section.paragraph: Working notes (hidden; not part of the submitted calculation): how this edition was produced, its tool status and the open bookkeeping items.

Journal edition written by scripts/build_ring_wall_bpad.py from the Pier Wall Design notebook package (ring_wall, the engine of Pier_Wall_Design.ipynb), starting case "D2 I-95 | Wall steel and welded pile rings", case SHA-256 bc5d7e9701d2615a3008a9e7b31b2d15cac017f06b243aa226f800fcc119cf8a, package source SHA-256 dc3550977246aa0511f7b5cbe389f7cd4662c1c5cc147f9b2c259b9cd0ff55b6. Every definition below was read back from this XML, evaluated by the independent Blockpad-syntax evaluator and compared with the notebook ledger to 1 part in 10⁹ (673 values, 178 check statuses) before the file was written. Native Blockpad recalculation, appearance review and engineering review were not performed; the equations are the notebook's and the ratios are not design acceptance.

Status: 1 FAILED CHECKS · LIMITED SCOPE. Failed checks: RING-GRID. Pending (contact lost) checks: 0; the notebook writes that status as PENDING, this edition as NO CONTACT (the word is reserved by the submission text rule).

Ring moment basis D-070 (21 October 2026): tributaries assign vertical force only; the radial placement tolerance is a rigid-body pile-group redistribution; the ring moment is the pile-head compatibility moment shared equally by the ring rows. The former R (|e_n| + Δ_p) moment is kept as M_s for comparison. Wall geometry D-075 (22 October 2026): the CAD pier wall, 219 × 36 in from EL 24.5264 (1 ft below terrain) to the cap bottom EL 40.76494 (194.8625 in high), 19.5 in from each wall end to the outer pile; the journal gravity sheet row 42 carries the same wall. Pile stiffness defaults come from the pier pile case (PILE-PIER-CASE): 20 in pipe, 92.4 in from the wall bottom to the equivalent fixity (110.7 in sand depth to fixity below the pile-case ground EL 26.05, LRFD C10.7.3.13.4, less the 18.3 in of wall below that ground), 600 in axial spring length as an allowance because the tip elevation is pending. The calculation is a tool edition of the notebook; the registered source is the project_current/pier_wall export.

• SHARING: Midplane tributaries assign vertical force and the ring rows share the pile-head moment equally; all rings are assumed to engage. Concrete transfer (including concrete below rings), splitting/breakout and row compatibility need a separately substantiated load path.

• STIFFNESS: Ring moments follow pile-head rotational stiffness against the rigid-wall rotation (D-070). The free length to fixity and the axial spring length are entered values (defaults from the pier pile case with sand depth to fixity, LRFD 10.7.3.13.4; tip elevation pending). Lateral, thermal, unsymmetric and construction-stage rotations enter only through the imposed rotation input.
• SCOPE: Wall checks cover minimum shrinkage/temperature steel and detailing only. Wall flexure, shear, lateral loads, seismic and strength load paths are outside this calculation.
• CONNECTION: Local plate and double-fillet checks do not establish pipe-shell bending/ovalization, global pile interaction, ring-segment splices, fatigue, corrosion or WPS/fabrication adequacy.

• BASIS: Confirm exposure/cover, material grades, construction joints and bar anchorage routing. Starting dimensions follow the CAD pier wall (219 x 36 in, bottom 1 ft below terrain at EL 24.5264, top at the cap bottom); the geometry notebook does not yet own the pier wall. The ring plate is 1/2 in by user selection (D-078; the thinnest plate with every check at or under 0.95 of its limit is 7/16 in, set by the maximum fillet at the ring edge); the CAD rings (D-076) are 3/4 in until reconciled.

This calculation covers the welded annular-ring support concept, the concept of the CAD model (D-076, D-079). The fin-plate and hairpin hanger concept (the former C006 Pier Wall, Hairpins and Fin Plates) was withdrawn from the project on 22 October 2026 (D-082, task T040) and is kept under sequestered/pier_wall_fins/ for revival; calculation numbers are permanent, so C006 is not reused.

report.paragraph: Design basis

Welded annular steel rings carry the self-weight of the 219 × 36 × 194.863 in concrete pier wall onto 4 steel pipe piles of 20 in diameter. Each pile carries 5 rows of annular plates welded with continuous fillets above and below; the wall concrete bears on the plates. This calculation checks full annular compression contact, concrete bearing, plate bending and shear at the pipe face, both fillets and the adjacent ring and pipe base metal, then the minimum shrinkage and temperature reinforcement, spacing, cover, laps and bar fit of the wall.

Load path. The gross wall prism is divided at midplanes between piles and between ring rows, clipped at the wall edges, and each cell's factored weight is the vertical force on its ring. The continuous wall carries the offset of a cell centroid from its pile; the ring moment is the compatibility moment of the pile head: the rigid wall rotates on the axial and rotational springs of the pile heads when the pile group is displaced by the radial placement tolerance, every pile head carries k_θ·θ_w, the ring rows share it equally, and the axial redistribution ΔR is added to each tributary reaction. The former basis, R·(|e_n| + Δ_p) at every ring, is evaluated as M_s for comparison only.

AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, 10th edition (2024): concrete bearing 5.6.5 with the resistance factor of 5.5.4.2 and no supporting-area enhancement (m = 1); minimum shrinkage and temperature reinforcement 5.10.6; bar spacing 5.10.3.1.1 and 5.10.3.2; bend diameter 5.10.2; development and Class B laps 5.10.8.2.1 and 5.10.8.4.3; fillet weld resistance, minimum and maximum size and length 6.13.3.2.4, 6.13.3.4 and 6.13.3.5; shear yielding and rupture of the adjacent ring and pipe metal 6.13.5.2 and 6.13.5.3; steel resistance factors 6.5.4.2; depth to fixity for the pile free length C10.7.3.13.4. Project cover, grid pitch cap and exposure follow the entered values and the FDOT Structures Manual.

Units are inches, kip and ksi; concrete density in kip/ft³; rotations in radians. Ring elevations locate the plate top above the wall bottom. Bearing excludes the footprint of the upper fillet; the peak pressure is applied over the whole radial cantilever strip; the two fillets form a couple over the plate thickness. Weld legs are specified in sixteenths of an inch. A check reads PASS when demand is within capacity and FAIL otherwise or when the available clearance is not positive; a ring whose minimum pressure is negative loses full contact and its bearing, plate, weld and base-metal checks read NO CONTACT: their values are trial values until contact is restored.

Outside this calculation: wall flexure, shear and lateral or seismic load paths; concrete splitting, breakout and the transfer below the lowest ring; pipe-shell bending and ovalization; global pile interaction, ring-segment splices, fatigue, corrosion and WPS or fabrication acceptance; confirmation of the pile stiffness lengths. The fin-plate and hairpin support concept (the former C006) was withdrawn from the project on 22 October 2026 and is not evaluated here.
